substantive_reconstruction.adjoint_and_phase: Define T=(1/4)Σ_P PρP†. Each chosen P∈{I,X,Y,Z} is Hermitian-unitary, so this equals the stated formula. For a unitary Pauli Q, QTQ†=(1/4)Σ_P (QP)ρ(QP)†; crucially (QP)†=P†Q†=PQ for the Hermitian representatives, not QP in general. Multiplication by Q permutes the four Pauli classes modulo scalar phases. Writing QP=ωP′, |ω|=1, gives ωP′ρconj(ω)P′†=P′ρP′†. Thus the correct sum is invariant.
substantive_reconstruction.commutant_and_trace: Invariance QTQ†=T implies QT=TQ. It extends from the representatives to the whole generated Pauli representation, including its central scalar phases. The stipulated irreducibility on finite-dimensional C² makes its commutant scalar by Schur, so T=λI. Trace cyclicity and P†P=I give trT=(1/4)Σ_P trρ=1. Since trI=2, λ=1/2. This uses no matrix-entry evaluation of the density input.
substantive_reconstruction.defect_and_boundaries: The predecessor's right factor (QP) instead of (QP)† is materially false: for Q=X and ρ=I/2 the incorrectly squared-product sum is zero because the Y,Z products have square −I, whereas the genuine conjugated sum is I/2. This finite witness diagnoses the omitted adjoint but is not the replacement proof. Individual QP need not be Hermitian; cancellation requires an adjoint phase, not ω²=1. The stated argument includes pure and mixed density matrices; positivity is not used to smuggle an extra rank or nonzero-entry premise.
